npmos.glossary.access-list.defaultMessage: Who may open a proxy host: allowed and denied addresses and/or a login and password.

npmos.glossary.acme.defaultMessage: Free certificates issued and renewed automatically. Needs access to the internet and a domain reachable from it; optional in NPMOS.

npmos.glossary.advanced-model.defaultMessage: A larger detection model of open-appsec, uploaded as a file on WAF → Agent.

npmos.glossary.agent.defaultMessage: The open-appsec service that takes requests from nginx and decides whether to let them through. Its state is on WAF → Agent.

npmos.glossary.air-gap.defaultMessage: NPMOS works without the internet; going out (ACME, updates, hub) is an option you switch on.

npmos.glossary.audit-log.defaultMessage: The record of who changed what and when. The history of a host is taken from it.

npmos.glossary.bouncer.defaultMessage: The part that enforces CrowdSec bans: here nginx of NPMOS and the WAF agent.

npmos.glossary.ca.defaultMessage: Certificate authority: the certificate that signs others. For mTLS it is the CA of your client certificates.

npmos.glossary.confidence.defaultMessage: From what confidence a request counts as an attack in Prevent: Critical blocks the least, Medium the most.

npmos.glossary.crowdsec.defaultMessage: Detects attackers from logs and bans their addresses. In NPMOS it runs locally, without the CrowdSec console.

npmos.glossary.dead-host.defaultMessage: A domain that answers 404: it is reserved but serves nothing, or a TLS certificate is kept for it.

npmos.glossary.decision.defaultMessage: A CrowdSec verdict about an address: ban or captcha, for a set time.

npmos.glossary.detect-learn.defaultMessage: The WAF logs attacks and learns from the traffic, but lets everything through. Start here.

npmos.glossary.fail-open.defaultMessage: What happens to requests when the agent does not answer in time: they pass without inspection (fail-open) or are refused (fail-close).

npmos.glossary.hsts.defaultMessage: Tells browsers to open the site only over HTTPS for a long time. Hard to undo: enable it when HTTPS works.

npmos.glossary.mtls.defaultMessage: Mutual TLS: besides the server, the client shows a certificate. Without a certificate signed by the selected CA the host does not open (Required) or the host gets to know it (Optional).

npmos.glossary.nginx.defaultMessage: The web server inside NPMOS that accepts all traffic and serves the hosts.

npmos.glossary.open-appsec.defaultMessage: The WAF built into NPMOS: a machine-learning engine instead of signature lists. Works locally, without its cloud.

npmos.glossary.policy.defaultMessage: The settings file of the agent. NPMOS generates it from the hosts; expert fragments are added on WAF → Policy (expert).

npmos.glossary.prevent-learn.defaultMessage: The WAF blocks attacks (403) and keeps learning. Switch to it when Detect shows no false positives.

npmos.glossary.proxy-host.defaultMessage: A domain that NPMOS accepts over HTTP(S) and passes to an internal service (the upstream). WAF, mTLS and access lists are set on proxy hosts.

npmos.glossary.redirect.defaultMessage: A domain that answers with a redirect (301, 302…) to another address.

npmos.glossary.severity.defaultMessage: How dangerous an event is, in the terms of the agent. Important events are Critical and High.

npmos.glossary.stream.defaultMessage: Forwarding of a TCP and/or UDP port without HTTP: databases, SSH, games. Shown in the hosts table as :port.

npmos.glossary.subtitle.defaultMessage: Terms that the interface keeps in English, and what they mean in NPMOS.

npmos.glossary.tls.defaultMessage: Encryption of the connection between the browser and NPMOS (HTTPS). SSL is its old name.

npmos.glossary.tuning.defaultMessage: The local open-appsec services that collect what the agent learned and suggest tuning. Replace its cloud.

npmos.glossary.upstream.defaultMessage: The address and port where a host forwards requests (the Destination column). NPMOS checks that it accepts connections.

npmos.glossary.waf.defaultMessage: Web application firewall: inspects HTTP requests and blocks attacks (SQL injection, XSS…). In NPMOS it is open-appsec.
